# Playbook: Content / Blog Site

A content-led site: articles, guides, documentation-style publications, where search discovery and reading experience are the product. Use this playbook for docs sites too (§5.6). If the site exists mainly to sell a product with accounts and billing, use the SaaS playbook instead.

## Goal

Ship a fast, indexable publication where every article traces to a brief and a named author, metadata and structured data match what is visibly on the page, Core Web Vitals budgets hold on article templates, WCAG 2.2 AA passes, and the site is deployed with monitoring and rollback.

## Departments and order

D1 → D2 → D3+D13+D4+D5 → D7+D8 → D6 → D9 — exactly as the §5.6 table; no deviation. D12 and D14 appear as explicit steps 5 and 6 per the §5.6 standing rule; D17 and D18 appear as conditional steps 4b and 6b.

## Docs to write first

Before any code, scaffold from `project-templates` and write:

- `requirements.md` — audience, content types, publishing workflow, and what the site must rank/be found for.
- `fact-sheet.md` — the publication's verifiable facts: author identities and credentials, publication details, any statistics the house style cites. No invented authors, credentials, or reader numbers.
- `stack.md` — CMS/rendering choice (static, headless CMS, or server-rendered) with dated criteria (G-AR-023).
- `progress.md`, `DECISIONS.md` — session log and decision record.
- `CONTENT_METADATA.md` — the content model: fields per content type, author attribution rules, review-by dates, metadata requirements per route.
- `SCHEMA.md` — content storage invariants if a database backs the CMS (draft/published states, slug uniqueness).
- `.env.example` — CMS and analytics credentials by name + purpose (§5.9).

## Step-by-step sequence

**Step 0 — Core and scaffold.** Load `bundles/core.md`; generate the project (G-PM-001, G-PM-002); write the docs above.

**Step 1 — Requirements (D1).** Fix the audience, the content types, who writes and who approves, and the publishing cadence the design must support. ◆ **DECISION — comments or reader accounts?** Either one pulls in moderation, auth, and a larger D14 register. If the user has not asked for them, the default is *no comments, no accounts* — record the decision in `requirements.md` rather than building the machinery "just in case." (Unattended run: BOOTSTRAP's approval-points rule applies at this point — a decision recorded in the commissioning brief or `requirements.md` counts as the answer; if none is recorded and no user is reachable, follow the §6.3 stuck protocol (log-and-continue, then the safe defaults) and record the substitution in `progress.md`.)

**Step 2 — Architecture (D2).** Choose the rendering/CMS stack by criteria recorded before the decision (G-AR-023): editorial workflow, build time at expected article count, hosting cost. A static or cached architecture is the default for content; a server-rendered app needs a written reason in `DECISIONS.md`.

**Step 3 — Build (D3+D13+D4+D5).** Content model first (`SCHEMA.md` / `CONTENT_METADATA.md`), templates second, sample content last — and sample content is written as real, publishable articles or clearly-marked draft fixtures, never lorem ipsum that survives to launch (G-QA-141). D13 inside the step: article typography and templates pass the contrast script (G-AC-011) and the criterion checklist (G-AC-015); long-form reading is the primary surface and gets the full keyboard + screen-reader audit (G-AC-002, G-AC-003).

**Step 4 — Content pipeline (D9 setup).** Stand up the `content-strategy` workflow now, while templates are fresh: every article starts from a brief (G-CO-041 brief traceability), metadata is linted in CI (G-CO-011), and the sitemap is generated from the route inventory, never hand-maintained (G-CO-091). Drafting itself happens continuously from here on; the launch gate is step 9.
**Step 4b — AI assistance (D17, conditional).** AI-drafted or AI-assisted articles are disclosed per the publication's stated policy in `fact-sheet.md`, pass the same claim-trace as human copy (G-CO-061), and any on-site AI feature passes `ai-safety` (G-AI-021). Undisclosed AI content presented as human reporting is a Real Content violation (§5.7 rank 3).

**Step 5 — Performance budgets (D12, explicit step).** Article templates carry the strictest budgets (they are the most-visited and most-linked pages): CI budget assertion (G-AN-101) and the field check on the 28-day p75 (G-AN-111) once live.

**Step 6 — Legal and privacy (D14, explicit step).** Register covers analytics, comments/accounts if present, newsletter data if present. Cookie consent with pre-consent scan (G-LG-041); legal documents diffed against the register (G-LG-031).

**Step 7 — Verification (D7+D8).** Even a static site gets the security pass: OWASP checklist review proportionate to the surface (G-SE-003), full-history secret scan (G-SE-041) — CMS tokens leak into repos constantly — placeholder sweep over every template and seed article (G-QA-141; scan rendered output, not source), and browser verification of the article, index, and search routes (G-QA-031 browser-verification gates).

**Step 8 — Deploy (D6, last build step).** Hosting selection and production checks (G-DO-071 external production check, G-DO-075 hosting record audit), pipeline with broken-test drill (G-DO-001), rollback drill (G-DO-151). Domain and DNS per `domains-dns` (G-DO-101 record-sheet match) and TLS per `ssl-certificates` (G-DO-111).

**Step 9 — Launch and discovery (D9).** The full content gate set on the production build: indexability diff (G-CO-001), route inventory crawl (G-CO-002), structured data validated and diffed against visible content (G-CO-081, G-CO-082), sitemap audit (G-CO-091), authorship audit — every byline resolves to a real person or an honest collective, and house bylines name an accountable team, not a fake individual (G-CO-044) — and claim-trace on launch articles (G-CO-061).

Family summary (§5.6): G-QA-* all green; G-AC-* WCAG 2.2 AA pass; G-CO-* SEO + structured-data validation pass.

## Failure handling

- **A gate fails:** fix in the owning step, re-run. Same failure twice → §6.3: log in `progress.md`, continue unblocked work, batch blockers with concrete options.
- **Structured data disagrees with the page (G-CO-082):** the launch waits. Markup that claims a different author, date, or headline than the visible page is a trust defect, not a typo — fix the generator, not the one instance.
- **Authorship or claim-trace fails (G-CO-044, G-CO-061):** the article does not publish. An invented expert byline or an untraceable statistic is a Real Content violation (§5.7 rank 3); there is no waiver without the user's explicit agreement, and the correct fix is a real author or a cut claim.
- **Two skills contradict:** §5.7 precedence (Real Content 3 and accessibility 5 both outrank content/SEO 14); log in `DECISIONS.md`.
- **A gate is itself wrong:** recorded waiver in `progress.md` + `DECISIONS.md` (§6.3 step 5), flagged as a repo gap.
- **A secret leaks:** revoke/rotate immediately, incident recorded without the value (§5.9 step 4).

## Definition of done

- Live on a real host/domain; G-DO-071 green; rollback drill on record; monitoring up (QB-02).
- Every launch article traces to a brief and a real named author; metadata lint, sitemap, and structured-data gates green on the production build.
- Article templates within budget in CI and, after 28 days, in field data (G-AN-111).
- Zero P0/P1 defects (QB-01); no placeholder text, fake authors, or untraceable claims anywhere on the site.
- `progress.md` and `handover.md` current; the publishing workflow (brief → draft → gates → publish) is documented in the project README so the user's next article follows it without the agent re-deriving it.
- **Pre-provisioning complete:** where no production environment exists yet, the project may be recorded as *pre-provisioning complete* — every gate except the provisioning-waived ones green, each waived gate recorded as a provisioning waiver per §6.3, and the unblocking conditions listed in `progress.md`. The deployment requirements above remain open until the environment exists; pre-provisioning complete is not done.

## Worked mini-example

Sample project: **Atlas Blog**, a travel-guide publication launching with 12 articles.

1. Step 0: core loaded; project scaffolded; CMS token and analytics ID listed in `.env.example` by name only.
2. Step 1: requirements fix guides + city pages, no comments, no accounts; decision recorded.
3. Step 2: criteria written first (editorial ease, build time at 500 articles, $0–10/mo hosting) → static generation with a headless CMS wins; decision logged (G-AR-023).
4. Step 3: content model defines guide fields and mandatory author attribution; article template passes contrast script and keyboard walk (G-AC-011, G-AC-002).
5. Step 4: briefs written for all 12 launch articles; metadata lint wired into CI (G-CO-011).
6. Step 5: article template budgeted at 150 KB JS / LCP 2.5 s (G-AN-101).
7. Step 6: register covers analytics + newsletter; consent scan shows the newsletter provider's script loading pre-consent — moved behind consent (G-LG-041).
8. Step 7: secret scan finds the CMS token in an early commit — token rotated, history noted, incident recorded in `progress.md`; placeholder sweep clean.
9. Step 8: deployed to production domain; DNS records match the record sheet (G-DO-101); rollback drill passes.
10. Step 9: one article's JSON-LD names a different author than its byline (G-CO-082 fail) — generator fixed to read the same author field, re-validated; authorship audit confirms all 12 bylines are real people (G-CO-044). Done.

# frontend-core

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/frontend/frontend-core/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/frontend.md`).*

## Rules

1. **FE-001 — Semantic structure first.** Landmarks, headings, and native controls come before any component styling; framework components wrap native elements, and custom widgets are the last resort. (WCPM §1 priority order, R-1.x.)
2. **FE-002 — A clickable `div` is a defect.** Anything that responds to a click is a `<button>` or `<a>` with a real href, keyboard-operable and focusable. There is no styling exception.
3. **FE-003 — Reserved media dimensions.** Every image and video ships with `width`/`height` or an `aspect-ratio` so nothing shifts after load; layout stability is part of the CLS budget, not a polish step.
4. **FE-004 — Tokens only.** No hard-coded color, spacing, radius, or duration values in page or component code — semantic tokens from design-tokens are the only source (FE-041).
5. **FE-005 — The budget is a requirement.** Each route carries a JavaScript budget and the Core Web Vitals bars at the 75th percentile. A feature that breaks the budget is redesigned or split, never shipped heavy. Thresholds are cited from the numbers registry in `gates/`, per WCPM Appendix F — not restated here or per project.
6. **FE-006 — Real imagery only.** Imagery depicts the actual product, place, or people, or is clearly generic decoration. AI artifacts in photography (malformed hands, gibberish in-image text, warped logos) are a blocker, never a shrug (DET-VIS-024).
7. **FE-007 — Render real data only.** The frontend renders data that exists: no invented logos in "trusted by" rows, no unsourced stat bands, no placeholder avatars presented as people (WCPM Appendix A data/fabrication bans, D- working IDs). A claim the data cannot support is removed, not decorated.
8. **FE-008 — In-UI copy follows the copy rules.** Interface text carries no banned filler adjectives or verification phrases (WCPM Appendix A.4/A.5 word lists, CC cures); labels name the action or the thing, in the product's own vocabulary.
9. **FE-009 — The rendering surface serves search honestly.** Titles, meta descriptions, and structured data are rendered from the page's real content (WCPM §10 rendering surface; G-SCH family is designed to pass here, content owned by D9). Metadata describing content the page does not contain is a fabrication, not SEO.
10. **FE-010 — Works degraded before it works pretty.** Every page must function at 320px wide, on keyboard alone, and with images or scripts failed, before visual enhancement is layered on. Enhancement is progressive by construction.

## Checklist

- [ ] Landmarks, headings, and native controls carry the page structure (FE-001).
- [ ] No clickable divs or spans anywhere (G-FE-002, FE-002).
- [ ] Every image/video reserves its dimensions; CLS stays within budget (FE-003).
- [ ] Lighthouse CI and bundle budget are green for this route, or the local form is recorded as a tool-form substitution (G-FE-001).
- [ ] axe-core reports zero critical violations (G-FE-002).
- [ ] No raw color/spacing/duration literals outside tokens (G-FE-003).
- [ ] Every image inspected at 100%; no AI artifacts, no fake marks (G-FE-004).
- [ ] Every rendered statistic traces to a source with a date (FE-007).

# content-strategy

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/seo-content/content-strategy/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/seo-content.md`).*

## Rules

1. **CO-081 — No brief, no draft.** Every piece of content starts from a brief naming its audience, goal, target query or intent, owner, and reviewer. A brief missing any of the five does not enter production, and no draft is written against an unwritten brief.
2. **CO-082 — Volume is an output, never a quota.** The plan never sets a pages-per-week or pages-per-month target. Output is whatever number of briefs clear the CO-081 bar; Google's scaled content abuse policy makes volume-for-rankings the violation regardless of whether humans or AI wrote the pages.
3. **CO-083 — One canonical page per topic.** The topic map assigns each topic to exactly one canonical page. A second page on the same topic is admitted only with a written differentiation: a different audience, format, or body of page-specific verified material the canonical page does not carry.
4. **CO-084 — The swap test for variants.** A location, keyword, or product variant page ships only with real page-specific data (staff, stock, pricing, regulations, local facts) such that swapping the keyword back would break the page. If two variants stay interchangeable after the swap, they are one page, not two.
5. **CO-085 — Every piece carries an owner and a review-by date.** At publication, each page records a named owner and the date by which its claims are re-verified. A page with no owner or no review-by date is not finished, however polished the copy.
6. **CO-086 — Authorship is real.** Pieces are credited to real people the publisher can evidence, or to an accountable house byline ("The Support Team"). Invented author personas — names, headshots, bios for people who do not exist — are never planned, briefed, or published.
7. **CO-087 — Decisions cite data.** Every brief, refresh, and retirement names the evidence behind it: Search Console query/page data, analytics landing-page evidence, or a documented audience need. "We should write about X" with no cited evidence is an opinion, and opinions do not enter the calendar.
8. **CO-088 — Topics stay inside the real offer.** The topic map covers only subjects the business can actually serve and evidence from its own operation. A topic the business has no product, service, data, or experience behind is out of scope, however much search demand it shows.
9. **CO-089 — Refresh or retire on schedule.** When a page's review-by date arrives, its owner re-verifies its claims and then refreshes, retires, or re-dates it with the verification recorded. Silently editing the date without re-verifying the content is not a refresh.
10. **CO-090 — The programmatic admission bar.** Templated or programmatic page sets are admitted only when every page in the set carries page-specific verified data passing CO-084. A set whose pages differ only in a swapped term is rejected at planning, not discovered at audit.
11. **CO-091 — Distribution is part of the brief.** A brief is incomplete until it names the page's planned inbound internal links and its distribution step (newsletter, social, partner, in-product). A page planned to be found "by the sitemap" is planned to be orphaned.
12. **CO-092 — Depth per topic over page count.** When a topic cannot support another substantively different page, the plan deepens the canonical page — new verified data, better coverage of the intent — instead of spawning a sibling. The plan records this choice so the refusal of volume is a decision on file, not an omission.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every item in production traces to a brief with audience, goal, intent, owner, and reviewer (G-CO-041).
- [ ] The plan states no pages-per-week or pages-per-month target anywhere (CO-082).
- [ ] Each topic maps to one canonical page; variants carry a written differentiation (CO-083).
- [ ] Every variant page passes the swap test with real page-specific data (CO-084).
- [ ] Every published page has a named owner and a review-by date (CO-085).
- [ ] All bylines are real people or an accountable house byline (G-CO-044).
- [ ] Each brief, refresh, and retirement cites the data behind it (CO-087).
- [ ] Similarity clustering shows no interchangeable page set (G-CO-042).

# technical-seo

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/seo-content/technical-seo/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/seo-content.md`).*

## Rules

1. **CO-001 — The indexable-page contract.** Every page intended for search returns HTTP 200, carries a self-referencing canonical, and is reachable by following links from the site itself. A page failing any leg is a defect to fix, not a ranking mystery to explain.
2. **CO-002 — Server-rendered by default.** Indexable content ships as server-rendered or statically generated HTML. Client-side rendering of indexable content is an exception that must be verified under CO-003, never a default.
3. **CO-003 — Verify the rendered HTML.** JavaScript-dependent content is checked in the rendered HTML (Search Console URL Inspection or an equivalent rendered-DOM fetch), never assumed from source code, view-source, or a local build.
4. **CO-004 — robots.txt discipline.** robots.txt follows RFC 9309 syntax, is served at the host root with HTTP 200, and never blocks the CSS or JavaScript assets that rendering the pages requires. Every change to it is reviewed like a code change.
5. **CO-005 — The promotion indexability diff.** Before every production release, staging and production are diffed on robots.txt, `noindex` (meta and X-Robots-Tag), basic-auth walls, and canonical host. Any staging protection found in production is a release blocker.
6. **CO-006 — One canonical URL per page.** Each page has exactly one canonical URL, stated as an absolute URL that itself returns 200 and is indexable. Parameter, filter, sort, session, and print variants canonicalize to the base URL or carry `noindex`; they are never indexable duplicates competing with it.
7. **CO-007 — Redirect hygiene.** Permanent moves use 301 or 308. Redirects are single-hop wherever the destination is known; a chain longer than two hops is fixed at the source, not documented and left.
8. **CO-008 — Real status codes.** Missing content returns a real 404 or 410. An error page served with HTTP 200 (a soft 404) is a defect, as is redirecting every removed URL to the homepage.
9. **CO-009 — One host, one scheme.** The site canonicalizes to a single host form (www or non-www) over HTTPS. Every other host/scheme combination 301-redirects to it, and canonicals, sitemaps, and internal links use only that form.
10. **CO-010 — The sitemap contract.** The XML sitemap lists only canonical, indexable URLs that return 200, is regenerated when routes change, stays within protocol limits (50,000 URLs / 50 MB per file, sitemap index beyond that), and is referenced in robots.txt. Generation itself belongs to the sitemaps skill; this rule is the contract it must satisfy.
11. **CO-011 — Directive consistency.** robots.txt, meta robots, X-Robots-Tag, and canonicals never contradict each other on the same URL, and no CDN, firewall, or hosting rule blocks search or AI crawlers that robots.txt allows — Google names CDN/hosting-level blocking as a real eligibility failure for its AI features.
12. **CO-012 — Coverage reviewed on a cadence.** Search Console coverage and indexing reports are reviewed on a fixed cadence (monthly at minimum) and the review is logged. Every spike in excluded or error URLs is triaged to a named cause. Reports state eligibility and defects found; they never state or imply a ranking guarantee.

## Checklist

- [ ] Promotion indexability diff is clean: no staging directive in production (G-CO-001).
- [ ] Every indexable URL returns 200 with a self-referencing canonical (G-CO-002).
- [ ] robots.txt is RFC 9309-valid and blocks no render asset (CO-004).
- [ ] Redirect chains are ≤2 hops; permanent moves are 301/308 (G-CO-003).
- [ ] Deleted URLs return a real 404/410 — no soft 404s (CO-008).
- [ ] JavaScript-dependent templates verified in rendered HTML (G-CO-004).
- [ ] Sitemap lists only canonical, indexable, 200 URLs (CO-010).
- [ ] This month's Search Console coverage review is logged, with no ranking guarantee stated (G-CO-005).

# hosting

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/devops-deployment/hosting/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/devops-deployment.md`).*

## Rules

1. **DO-141 — The host decision is recorded.** The hosting record names the provider and plan, region(s), scaling behavior, sleep policy, bandwidth and build caps, and the exit path, each with the date it was checked against the provider's own documentation. A host chosen without this record is not chosen yet.
2. **DO-142 — Every deployment carries a posture tier.** Each deployment is labeled validation posture or production posture in the hosting record. The record names the promotion trigger (first real user, first payment, first availability commitment) and lists which detection parameters are knowingly waived at validation posture.
3. **DO-143 — No unrecorded single point of failure.** A production-posture deployment with availability requirements does not run as a single instance with its database on the same host unless that risk is a recorded decision in the hosting record with a named exit path.
4. **DO-144 — Health checks reflect the ability to serve.** The app exposes a readiness endpoint that fails when a required dependency (database, cache, queue) is unreachable, and the platform's health check points at it. A probe aimed at the homepage or any static page does not satisfy this rule.
5. **DO-145 — Ephemeral filesystems hold no state.** On a platform whose filesystem is reset by redeploys or spin-downs, user uploads and the application database live in external stores (object storage, managed database), never in local files or a local database file.
6. **DO-146 — Platform config is the IaC of record.** The provider's config file (for example `netlify.toml`, `render.yaml`, `fly.toml`, `vercel.json`) is committed to the repo, and the console matches it. Any difference between console and committed config is drift and is reconciled the same day it is found.
7. **DO-147 — Debug and admin surfaces stay closed.** Production runs with framework debug mode off, error responses contain no stack traces, and `/.git`, `/.env`, admin, and metrics paths are unreachable publicly or sit behind authentication plus network restriction.
8. **DO-148 — Host defaults are hardened.** Directory listing is off, server and framework version banners are suppressed, default welcome pages and unused virtual hosts are removed, and only the ports the application needs are open.
9. **DO-149 — Auth endpoints are throttled at the edge.** Rate-limit rules at the CDN, WAF, or gateway cover login, password-reset, and signup paths before launch, with stricter limits for unauthenticated traffic.
10. **DO-150 — Production is a separate environment.** Production has its own data store and its own credentials; staging and production resolve to different database hosts, and production data is never the test fixture.
11. **DO-151 — Production is verified from outside.** After every deploy, the public production URL is loaded over valid HTTPS from a network other than the deploy network, and the live deployment's commit SHA is confirmed equal to the repo HEAD and written into progress.md.
12. **DO-152 — The host-limit sheet stays current.** Caps that can stop the app (sleep behavior, bandwidth, build minutes, instance hours, expiring resources such as free databases) are recorded with their expiry or reset dates and re-checked against provider documentation at least every 90 days.

## Checklist

- [ ] Hosting record is complete: provider, region, scaling, sleep policy, caps, exit path, check date (DO-141).
- [ ] Posture tier is declared, with its promotion trigger and waived parameters (DO-142).
- [ ] No unrecorded single point of failure in production posture (DO-143, G-DO-075).
- [ ] Readiness fails in staging when the database is stopped (G-DO-072).
- [ ] Exposure probes are blocked and no version banners are served (G-DO-073).
- [ ] External check passes and the live commit SHA equals repo HEAD (G-DO-071).
- [ ] Console settings diff clean against the committed platform config (G-DO-074).

## Gate criteria digest — every gate this playbook cites

Generated from the owning skills: each cited gate's Check criterion, condensed to its first sentence(s) where long, and its Pass criterion complete and exact. Fail actions and full procedures live in the owning skill and in the department bundles. This digest ships at every rung — it is what makes this bundle the default complete load for the walk (BOOTSTRAP.md step 3).

### requirements-writing (`skills/product-requirements/requirements-writing/SKILL.md`)

- **G-PR-031 — Requirement lint.** Check: automated — run a script over the requirements file confirming (a) ID, source, priority, rationale, and verification method are present and non-empty for 100% of requirements, (b) each requirement contains exactly one "shall", and (c) every banned vague term is flagged unless its sentence contains a number or unit. Pass: zero violations.
- **G-PR-032 — Traceability coverage.** Check: automated — generate the coverage report: every Must-priority requirement has at least one linked source need and at least one linked acceptance criterion or test. Pass: 100% coverage.

### stack-selection (`skills/architecture/stack-selection/SKILL.md`)

- **G-AR-023 — Criteria predates decision.** Check: manual — in git history, confirm the criteria table exists at or before the commit that records the decision, the table scores every candidate on the same criteria, and the ADR names a rejected alternative and accepted downsides. Pass: all three hold.

### frontend-core (`skills/frontend/frontend-core/SKILL.md`)

- **G-FE-002 — Accessibility floor scan.** Check: automated — axe-core run over key routes. Pass: zero critical violations (automated) or zero findings under the manual form.

### wcag (`skills/accessibility-i18n/wcag/SKILL.md`)

- **G-AC-011 — Palette contrast computed by script.** Check: run the project contrast script (e.g. `node scripts/check-contrast.mjs design-tokens.json`), which parses every text/background and component-boundary token pair — including hover, focus, placeholder, and error states — and computes the WCAG ratio from the actual hex values. Pass: every normal-text pair ≥4.5:1, every large-text and non-text pair ≥3:1, zero pairs skipped.
- **G-AC-015 — Per-release criterion checklist for changed screens.** Check: open the release checklist; for each changed screen, confirm every criterion its changes touch is marked met / not met with the verifying method named (script, CI, or manual pass). Pass: zero unmarked affected criteria, and the target line still reads "WCAG 2.2 Level AA" (or the recorded pinned version).
- **G-AC-012 — Automated criterion rules pass in CI.** Check: run axe-core in CI over the changed screens (`npx @axe-core/cli <changed URLs>` or the project CI job) and confirm the rules mapped to 4.1.2, 1.1.1, and label criteria report zero violations. Pass: zero violations on the mapped rule set (automated) or zero unmet criteria under the manual form.

### accessibility-audit (`skills/accessibility-i18n/accessibility-audit/SKILL.md`)

- **G-AC-002 — Keyboard walk completed.** Check: manual pass — complete each primary process keyboard-only (Tab/Shift+Tab/Enter/Space/arrow keys/Esc), logging every trap, invisible focus stop, and lost-focus event against its criterion. Pass: a completed keyboard-walk checklist exists for every primary process, with findings registered.
- **G-AC-003 — Screen-reader smoke test completed.** Check: manual pass — run the primary journeys in at least one real screen reader (e.g. Pass: a dated smoke-test record names the AT/browser versions used and lists pass/fail per journey.

### schema-design (`skills/database/schema-design/SKILL.md`)

- **G-DB-001 — Schema lint.** Check: automated — CI queries the live catalog of the migrated test database and fails on any violation of the invariant: every table has a primary key, every foreign key column is indexed, and every index and constraint the schema declares exists in the live catalog. Pass: zero findings.

### content-strategy (`skills/seo-content/content-strategy/SKILL.md`)

- **G-CO-041 — Brief traceability audit.** Check: automated — diff the published URL inventory against the brief register; every published URL must map to a brief containing audience, goal, intent, owner, reviewer, and a cited evidence source. Pass: 100% of published URLs trace to a complete brief.
- **G-CO-044 — Authorship audit.** Check: manual — list every byline on the site; for each individual byline, require an author page plus one independent trace (staff page, professional profile); house bylines must name an accountable team, not a fake individual. Pass: every byline resolves to a real person or an honest collective.

### technical-seo (`skills/seo-content/technical-seo/SKILL.md`)

- **G-CO-001 — Promotion indexability diff.** Check: automated — script fetches staging and production robots.txt plus the response headers and meta robots of the top route templates, and diffs directives and canonical host. Pass: zero staging protections (noindex, Disallow: /, auth wall, staging canonical) present in production.
- **G-CO-002 — Route inventory crawl.** Check: automated — crawl the production route inventory and assert, per indexable URL: HTTP 200, self-referencing canonical in the canonical host form, no `noindex`. Pass: 100% of indexable URLs satisfy all three.

### on-page-seo (`skills/seo-content/on-page-seo/SKILL.md`)

- **G-CO-011 — Metadata lint.** Check: automated CI lint over the route inventory — extract every indexable page's `<title>` and meta description and fail on duplicates, missing values, or placeholder strings: `grep -rhoP '(?<=<title>).*?(?=</title>)' dist/ | sort | uniq -d` returns nothing, and the same for descriptions. Pass: zero duplicates, zero missing, zero defaults.

### structured-data (`skills/seo-content/structured-data/SKILL.md`)

- **G-CO-081 — CI schema validation.** Check: automated — on every build, fetch one sample URL per page type from the staging build, extract each `application/ld+json` block, parse it as JSON, and validate required properties per type against Google's rich-result requirements (Rich Results Test during development). Pass: every block parses and carries all required properties.
- **G-CO-082 — Markup-vs-visible diff.** Check: automated — script diffs `aggregateRating`, `price`, `datePublished`/`dateModified`, and `author` values in JSON-LD against the rendered page text for the same sample URLs. Pass: zero fields without an identical visible counterpart (page-external fields checked against fact-sheet.md per CO-172).

### sitemaps (`skills/seo-content/sitemaps/SKILL.md`)

- **G-CO-091 — Sitemap audit script.** Check: automated — `python3 scripts/sitemap_audit.py --sitemap https://example.com/sitemap.xml` fetches the sitemap (following the index to every shard), requests every listed URL (or a statistically sound random sample above 10,000 URLs), and asserts per URL: HTTP 200, no redirect, canonical tag equal to the listed URL, no `noindex` in meta robots or X-Robots-Tag, host and scheme equal to the canonical host. Pass: zero assertion failures.

### ai-safety (`skills/ai-features/ai-safety/SKILL.md`)

- **G-AI-021 — Red-team injection suite.** Check: in CI, run the feature's versioned red-team set against the staging build — direct payloads as user messages, indirect payloads embedded in fixture documents and pages — e.g. `npm run redteam -- --feature support-chat` (the project's runner). Pass: no critical payload executes an embedded instruction, reveals any part of the system prompt, or triggers a tool call; results are stored with the release.

### performance-budgets (`skills/analytics-observability/performance-budgets/SKILL.md`)

- **G-AN-101 — CI budget assertion.** Check: `lhci autorun` runs in the merge pipeline with the `assert` block and `budget.json` from the repo, collecting at least three runs per template and asserting the median. Pass: exit code 0 on every template.

### core-web-vitals (`skills/analytics-observability/core-web-vitals/SKILL.md`)

- **G-AN-111 — Field report check.** Check: automated — a scheduled job queries the RUM store for the trailing 28 days and emits, per template in the inventory and per device class, the p75 of LCP, INP, and CLS against the thresholds (LCP ≤ 2.5 s, INP ≤ 200 ms, CLS ≤ 0.1). Pass: every key template is "good" on all three vitals, or carries an open defect under AN-232.

### privacy-laws (`skills/legal-privacy/privacy-laws/SKILL.md`)

- **G-LG-001 — Register coverage check.** Check: script the register against product config and the data map — every market in config and every processing purpose in the data map must have a register row with non-empty regime, lawful-basis, and owner fields. Pass: zero uncovered markets or purposes.

### legal-documents (`skills/legal-privacy/legal-documents/SKILL.md`)

- **G-LG-031 — Document-vs-register diff.** Check: in CI, extract the processor names and data categories named in the privacy notice and diff them against the processor register and the RoPA; repeat for every served locale/surface variant. Pass: zero names or categories present in one source and absent from the other.

### cookie-consent (`skills/legal-privacy/cookie-consent/SKILL.md`)

- **G-LG-041 — Pre-consent network scan.** Check: a headless browser with a fresh profile loads the key pages with no interaction; capture every cookie set and every third-party request. Pass: zero non-essential cookies set and zero non-essential third-party requests fired before consent.

### owasp (`skills/security/owasp/SKILL.md`)

- **G-SE-003 — Top 10 checklist review.** Check: manual, checklist-driven — walk the release's Top 10 record line by line; each category shows a control, a code/config location, a test, and versioned ASVS IDs where cited. Pass: all ten categories complete, N/A entries carry written reasons.

### placeholder-scan (`skills/qa-testing/placeholder-scan/SKILL.md`)

- **G-QA-141 — Static sweep clean.** Check: automated — run the versioned pattern list over the rendered production output (built pages and shipped strings), e.g. `rg -i -n "lorem|ipsum|dolor sit amet|example\.com|example@|555-01|coming soon|content to follow" dist/` plus the template-syntax and stub-marker patterns from the pattern file; exclude documented code-sample contexts. Pass: exit 0 with zero unallow-listed hits.

### browser-verification (`skills/qa-testing/browser-verification/SKILL.md`)

- **G-QA-031 — Route smoke pass.** Check: automated — `npx playwright test smoke/routes.spec.ts` loads every route in the project's route list and fails on any console error, any response ≥400, or a blank render; the command's exit code is the verdict. Pass: exit 0 with the route count matching the route list.

### hosting (`skills/devops-deployment/hosting/SKILL.md`)

- **G-DO-071 — External production check.** Check: automated — `curl -sI https://<production-domain>/` from a network other than the deploy network returns 200 over a valid certificate, and the provider's deployment record shows a commit SHA equal to `git rev-parse HEAD`. Pass: both true.
- **G-DO-075 — Hosting record audit.** Check: manual — open the hosting record and confirm provider, region, scaling behavior, sleep policy, caps, exit path, posture tier, any single-point-of-failure decision, and a check date no more than 90 days old are all present. Pass: every field present and current.

### ci-cd (`skills/devops-deployment/ci-cd/SKILL.md`)

- **G-DO-001 — Broken-test drill (automated).** Check: open a throwaway pull request with a deliberately failing test; query the check-run status via the platform API and confirm the required check concludes `failure` and the branch ruleset reports merge blocked. Pass: check is red and merge is refused.

### rollback (`skills/devops-deployment/rollback/SKILL.md`)

- **G-DO-151 — Staging rollback drill.** Check: in staging, deploy a deliberately broken version, then execute the exact rollback command written in the runbook (for example `kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name>`) and time it; confirm both revisions appear in rollout/deploy history. Pass: previous version serves healthy traffic within the stated target time.

### domains-dns (`skills/devops-deployment/domains-dns/SKILL.md`)

- **G-DO-101 — Record-sheet match.** Check: automated — run `dig +short <domain> A`, `dig +short www.<domain> CNAME`, and `dig +short www.<domain> A` after every change and quarterly; diff the output against the committed record sheet. Pass: every returned value matches the sheet exactly.

### ssl-certificates (`skills/devops-deployment/ssl-certificates/SKILL.md`)

- **G-DO-111 — External TLS scan.** Check: run `testssl.sh <domain>` (or the SSL Labs scan) at launch and after any TLS change. Pass: TLS 1.2/1.3 only (any legacy protocol matches a dated exception in the project notes), full chain presented, grade and protocol list recorded.

### secrets-management (`skills/security/secrets-management/SKILL.md`)

- **G-SE-041 — Full-history secret scan.** Check: run `gitleaks git .` in CI over the complete git history on every pull request and before release. Pass: zero findings; placeholder hits in `.env.example` are confirmed fake per SE-082 and allowlisted individually.

### real-content (`skills/seo-content/real-content/SKILL.md`)

- **G-CO-061 — Claim-trace audit.** Check: run `python3 scripts/claim-trace.py --pages dist/ --fact-sheet fact-sheet.md` — the script extracts checkable facts (numbers, prices, dates, names) from the rendered pages and diffs them against fact-sheet.md, exiting non-zero on any unmatched or contradicted fact. Pass: exit code 0; every extracted fact traces to a fact-sheet entry.

### project-templates (`skills/project-memory/project-templates/SKILL.md`)

- **G-PM-001 — Manifest diff.** Check: generate a fresh project into a scratch directory and run `diff <(cd <output> && find . -type f | sort) <repo>/templates/mandated-manifest-<type>.txt` — the manifest shipped in this repository's `templates/` directory, never a locally reconstructed copy. Pass: zero differences, or every difference matched by a not-applicable entry with a reason in the generation record.
- **G-PM-002 — Unreplaced-token and marker scan.** Check: `grep -rn '{{' <output>/` and `grep -rn 'TODO\|FIXME' <output>/` — both must return nothing. Pass: zero hits.
